header.title: How to Replace Freon in a Leaky Refrigerator
header.description: This guide provides instructions on how to identify a refrigerant leak in a refrigerator and subsequently replace the lost Freon. It covers the process from diagnosis to adding refrigerant and oil, enabling a DIY repair.

steps.description: This step involves diagnosing potential issues causing a refrigerator to not cool properly before assuming a refrigerant leak.
actions: Inspect the air intake grill to ensure it is free of debris.
Check the vents on the back of the freezer compartment for blockages.
Clean the coil behind or under the fridge.
Verify the thermostat is working properly.
Look for an oily substance at the bottom of the appliance to detect a refrigerant leak.
Consider if the appliance has been punctured, which could indicate a refrigerant leak.
steps.part: air intake grill, vents, coil, thermostat, bottom of the appliance

steps.description: This step instructs the user to purchase the correct type of refrigerant to repair and replenish a coolant leak, considering potential restrictions and refrigerant types based on the refrigerator's manufacturing date.
actions: Determine if the problem is a coolant leak.
Identify the type of refrigerant needed (R-12 or R-134a).
Purchase the correct refrigerant based on the refrigerator's manufacturing date and local regulations.
Ensure the refrigerant type is correct to avoid damaging the compressor.

steps.description: Install a saddle valve on the large copper pipe coming from the refrigerator's compressor to allow for future coolant addition.
actions: Determine Freon system location using owner's manual.
Locate the compressor.
Install a saddle valve on the large copper pipe coming from the compressor.
Fasten the valve with two screws while it punctures the copper pipe.

steps.description: Vacuum air from the system using a specialized pump.
actions: open system
vacuum air
use special pump

steps.description: This step involves adding refrigerant (Freon) to the system using a hose connected to a saddle valve.
actions: Locate the proper refrigerant type in the owner’s manual.
Place a hose onto the saddle valve.

steps.description: Add a few tablespoons of PAG oil to lubricate the compressor.
actions: Add PAG oil
Refer to manual for exact amount
Add about five tablespoons
